rules_evaluated.evidence: L22: "The setup prompt copies them across, so what you built in Module 1<!--flag:module:earn-the-trust--> and Module 3<!--/flag:module:earn-the-trust--> comes with you." 'Them' = the two gitignored items just named in the same sentence, `CLAUDE.local.md` AND `observations/`. Checked against the project's own canonical training-architecture doc per this template's instruction ("Check against ... curriculum/trainings/<training>/training-architecture.md if relevant"): `training-architecture.md:36` — "observations/  # observations + business-rules notes; introduced at M4"; this file's own parent module (`learn-from-the-test.md:215`) — "M4's `walk-and-send-off` is the real producer; M5 adds none by design"; and `open-the-side-quest.md:86` — "M3 most often runs before M4, where `observations/` is first authored. At M3 the folder usually doesn't exist and the student has never met it." Three independent canonical sources agree `observations/` is an M4 artifact. Naming "Module 1 and Module 3" as the source of what's carried — while never naming Module 4, the module this exercise is literally forking FROM ("the commit your un-packaged run started at") and the module that produces one of the two named files — misstates provenance for the reader in the file's own subtitle claim ("carry the evidence"). Separately verified: `CLAUDE.local.md`'s M1+M3 framing is independently accurate (`earn-the-trust.md:180`: "M4 onward sees M3's rule additions as part of personal context"), so the defect is specific to `observations/` riding along on that pairing, not a wholesale invention.

The earlier merge-base wording this rule flagged at the prior pin ("it is where the run started") is no longer present — current L41 already reads "a commit or two before the run started, carrying the same code," matching the maintainer's dated accept-note (L57) that the approximation is deliberate and verified.
